attempted_claim: Let O_2^{333}, O_3^{333} be the orientable (3,3,3)-cusped prism orbifolds of Deblois–Gharagozlou–Hoffman, Table 2 — O_2^{333}=(3,3,2,3,3,4,2,2,3), O_3^{333}=(3,3,2,3,3,4,2,3,2) — proved minimal in their commensurability classes. How many hyperbolic knot complements S^3\K lie in each of the two commensurability classes, i.e. cover O_2^{333} resp. O_3^{333}? In particular, are the degree-312 and degree-528 examples tilde M_{i,1}, tilde M_{i,2} of Theorem 4.1 (plus chiral twins / geodesic-surface mutants) the only knot complements in each class, so each class contains at most three knot complements up to orientation-preserving isometry and mirroring, as the Reid–Walsh conjecture predicts?
decisive_failure: No complete enumeration, finiteness proof, or Reid-Walsh at-most-three verification for the O_2^{333}/O_3^{333} commensurability classes is claimed. The index-24 census figures and minimality facts cited are published results used only as evidence of blockage, not as new claims. Higher-index enumeration and any hidden-symmetry counting theorem remain beyond this pass.
